(anchor: "One concept must have one semantic identity. And conversely: One word must not silently represent multiple concepts.")
- `[S1420]` types=[DEFINITION, FORMALIZATION] scope=OBJECT — "Assembles the candidate canonical vocabulary as a twelve-symbol tuple (Identity, State, Observation, Evidence, Proposition, Assessment, Model, Uncertainty, Authority, Decision, Action, Lineage) plus Transition/Process/Invariant as structural mechanisms operating over them -- the basis to be challenged term by term." (anchor: "\mathcal K = (I,S,O,E,P,A,M,U,R,D,X,L) with: Transition, Process, Invariant as structural mechanisms operating over these concepts.")
- `[S1420]` types=[INVARIANT, DEFINITION] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "Canonical definition of Identity ('which thing are we talking about?'): identity remains stable across state changes (x_t=x_{t+1} while State(x_t)!=State(x_{t+1})); grounds invariant I_70 that a state transition must never silently change the subject's identity." (anchor: "I_{70}: A state transition must not silently change the identity of the subject.")
- `[S1420]` types=[DEFINITION, DISTINCTION] scope=OBJECT — "Canonical definition of State ('what is the condition of the domain object at time t?'): explicitly not the same as History, which is the full sequence of states." (anchor: "CurrentState\neq History. History is a sequence: H_x=(S_0,S_1,\ldots,S_n).")
- `[S1420]` types=[DEFINITION] scope=OBJECT — "Canonical definition of Observation ('what was observed?') as the tuple (subject,time,observer,content); an observation is an event of perception/measurement that does not automatically constitute truth." (anchor: "O=(subject,time,observer,content). ... Observation \not\Rightarrow Truth.")
- `[S1420]` types=[DEFINITION] scope=OBJECT — "Canonical definition of Evidence ('what information is being used to support or challenge a proposition?'), naming seven possible origins and requiring provenance; connects via supports/contradicts edges to Proposition." (anchor: "Evidence may originate from: observation; document; measurement; system event; human testimony; validated AI output; derived computation. But evidence requires provenance.")
- `[S1420]` types=[DEFINITION, DISTINCTION] scope=OBJECT — "Canonical definitions of Proposition (the claim itself, e.g. 'Deployment D completed successfully') and Assessment (Assessment=f(Proposition,Evidence,Model,Uncertainty), the current evaluation of the claim, drawn from {Supported,Refuted,Unknown,Ambiguous,Conflicted}) as two distinct concepts that must never be conflated." (anchor: "Proposition \neq Assessment. The proposition is the claim. The assessment is our current evaluation of that claim.")
- `[S1420]` types=[DEFINITION] scope=OBJECT — "Canonical definition of Model ('under what interpretation or formal assumptions are we evaluating the evidence?') as (Assumptions,Rules,Parameters), with model identity/version required to be tracked in lineage since different models can legitimately produce different assessments from the same evidence." - `[S1420]` types=[DEFINITION, DISTINCTION] scope=OBJECT — "Canonical definitions of Decision ('what choice was made?', not implying correctness) and Action ('what was actually done?', distinct from Decision), illustrated by an approved-but-unexecuted deployment."
